title: Hairpin lace table runner
subtitle: A narrow table runner in DK cotton made from joined hairpin lace strips.
excerpt: Three narrow hairpin lace strips joined along their inner edges make a table runner with an open loopy centre and a cotton fibre that launders well. Worked in DK cotton on a 5 cm frame.
sourceNotes: Hairpin lace table runners in cotton are a documented domestic needlework project from early 20th-century pattern books. This strip count, length, and border treatment are original to Homemade.

glossaryTerms.definition: A crochet technique where yarn is looped around a U-shaped metal frame while a central chain is worked with a hook, producing a strip of looped fabric on each side.
A crochet row that links the loops from two adjacent hairpin lace strips together, creating a seam between them.
A decorative border made by working a small chain loop and slip-stitching it closed between stitches along an edge.

crochet.gaugeText: 14 loops per 10 cm of strip length on a 5 cm wide frame in DK cotton.
crochet.finishedSizeText: Table runner approximately 28 cm wide x 120 cm long.

Work each strip with 1 double crochet per rotation on a 5 cm frame. Each strip needs 168 loops per side (120 cm at 14 loops per 10 cm). Make 3 strips in total.
Lay strips side by side. Join strip 1 to strip 2 with a joining row picking up one loop from each strip per double crochet. Join strip 2 to strip 3 the same way.

At each short end, work a picot edge: 1 double crochet into the first end loop, then work ch 3, slip stitch into the first chain (picot made), 1 double crochet into the next loop, repeat across. Weave in all ends with your tapestry needle. Block flat with light steam.
